sn34.19:1.5: One meditator is skilled in doing what’s conducive to immersion but not in entering immersion.
sn34.19:1.6: One meditator is skilled neither in entering immersion nor in doing what’s conducive to it.
sn34.19:1.7: One meditator is skilled both in entering immersion and in doing what’s conducive to it.
sn34.19:1.8: Of these, the meditator skilled both in entering immersion and in doing what’s conducive to it is the foremost, best, leading, highest, and finest of the four.
sn34.19:1.9: just as, mendicants, from a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these;
sn34.19:1.10: In the same way, mendicants, the meditator skilled both in entering immersion and in doing what’s conducive to it is the foremost, best, leading, highest, and finest of the four.”
